description:
Call this tool to find flights once the traveler has told you their dates: one way or round trip, up to two dates each way joined with _ (2026-11-20_2026-11-21), and up to three airports on each side.

Before you call it, you need four things: where they fly from, where to, the date they leave and, for a round trip, the date they come back. Ask for everything missing in one question. Do not pick dates for the traveler, and do not guess one way or round trip: "what is the cheapest flight from Newark to Los Angeles" still needs both. Search as soon as you have the four.

No dates yet: offer add_flight_bucket_list, which watches the route and alerts them when a good fare appears; use it when they want alerts over flexible months.

Fill in origin, destination, depart_date and, for a round trip, return_date, and you can also pass the traveler's own words in query and leave the fields you do not know empty: SlickTrip fills in only what their words say and guesses nothing else.

The answer lists priced itineraries, cheapest first, each with an itinerary_id for track_flight and search_return_flights, and a search_url. Then offer ways to narrow the choice: cabin, stops, airlines, times of day.

Leg.description: One leg of a multi-city trip.

destination.description: One airport or city code (JFK, NYCA) or a clear place name. For a city, send the city, not one of its airports.

origin.description: One airport or city code (JFK, NYCA) or a clear place name. For a city, send the city, not one of its airports.

airlines.description: Only these marketing carriers, as IATA codes or names.

arrive_after.description: HH:MM, local time at that airport.

arrive_before.description: HH:MM, local time at that airport.

carry_on_bags.description: Carry-on bags per traveler; prices then include the bag fees, as price_with_bags next to the fare.

checked_bags.description: Checked bags per traveler; fees are priced only for flights within the US and Canada (elsewhere the answer says they are not included). Prices then include them, as price_with_bags next to the fare.

connecting_airports.description: Only itineraries that change planes at these airports (codes or city codes), nonstops included: for 'US connections only' name the hubs.

currency.description: The currency the traveler wants prices in: USD, CAD, EUR, GBP, ILS, INR or JPY. Send it when the traveler names a currency or their words show where they live (euros for someone in Spain, or writing in French from Lyon). Empty answers in US dollars, or in the currency the traveler picked on SlickTrip. Amounts you send in (max_price_usd, target_price_usd, a price per night) stay US dollars.

depart_after.description: HH:MM, local time at that airport.

depart_before.description: HH:MM, local time at that airport.

depart_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. More dates joined with _ search them all as flexible dates (2026-11-03_2026-11-04): about 4 each way on a round trip, or up to 8 one way when the other has 1 or 2.

destination.description: Airport code (JFK), city code for all its airports (NYCA, LOND, ROME, TYOA) or a clear place name; up to 3 joined with _ (JFK_EWR). For a city, send the city (its name or code), not one of its airports: one can miss the cheapest or only flights. Unsure: call find_places.

display.description: compact: one line per option, more options, far fewer tokens; full: every field (what the cards draw). Empty: compact when the app shows no cards, full when it does.

exclude_airlines.description: Leave out itineraries with any flight sold by these carriers (IATA codes, names or an alliance), by flight number or airline name: for 'not Gol' or 'avoid Air India'.

exclude_connecting_airports.description: Leave out itineraries that change planes at these airports (codes or city codes).

lap_infants.description: Babies under 2 who will sit on an adult's lap (no seat of their own). Not counted in travelers and not in the quoted fare; the answer says how airlines charge them.

legs.description: Multi-city trip: the legs in order, each one place per side and one date. When given, origin, destination, depart_date and return_date are ignored.

lower_emissions.description: Only itineraries with lower emissions than is typical for the route.

max_duration_hours.description: Longest itinerary to show, in hours.

max_layover_hours.description: Longest layover allowed at every connection, in hours (half hours allowed): for 'layovers no longer than 5 hours'.

max_price_usd.description: Highest fare to show, USD, as the TOTAL for all travelers: for a per-person budget, multiply by travelers (2 at $300 each = 600). A bucket list's price bar is per traveler instead.

max_stops.description: Most stops allowed: 0 nonstop, 1, or 2 (2 or more: any number).

min_layover_hours.description: Shortest layover allowed at every connection, in hours (half hours allowed): for 'at least 2 hours to connect'.

no_overnight_layovers.description: Leave out itineraries with an overnight layover: for 'no overnight at the transit airport'.

origin.description: Airport code (JFK), city code for all its airports (NYCA, LOND, ROME, TYOA) or a clear place name; up to 3 joined with _ (JFK_EWR). For a city, send the city (its name or code), not one of its airports: one can miss the cheapest or only flights. Unsure: call find_places.

query.description: The traveler's request in their own words, used to fill any field left empty.
examples: JFK to Lisbon the first week of October, business

return_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD for a round trip; empty for one way. More dates joined with _, as for depart_date.

travelers.description: Travelers who need a seat (adults and children); fares are for all of them together. One booking holds up to 9 (a larger group gets a suggested split). A baby under 2 on a lap is not counted here.

user_request.description: Optional, and it works in the traveler's favor. Quote the traveler's latest message about this trip exactly as they wrote it (their wording, language and spelling), not a summary: when a search fails or comes back empty, SlickTrip compares their words with the arguments sent and returns a corrected search, so you can fix it without asking again (it has caught Cancun sent as MEX, and travelers dropped from the party). If the message only answers a question ("yes, the 20th"), quote the one that asked for the trip. Send the same quote on every call for this request. Leave out anything not about the trip, and never names, contact details, or payment or ID information. The words also help SlickTrip improve its search.
examples: necesito llevar a mi mamá de Calgary a Kolkata a fines de octubre, no puede hacer escala en Estados Unidos

name: search_flights

code.description: On an error: a machine-readable kind, e.g. unknown_place

filters.description: Filters as the caller gave them (max_stops, airlines, max_price_usd, ...)

highlights.description: The spread over every matching fare: cheapest, cheapest_nonstop, fastest, earliest, latest; each with itinerary_id, price, airlines, stops, duration_minutes, departs_at

itineraries.description: Items: itinerary_id, price {total_usd, per_traveler_usd}, outbound leg, needs_leg, track_url, optional depart_date + search_key

message.description: Error or sign-in message from the server wrapper

note.description: Guidance on trip type or why empty

places_assumed.description: Place names this call resolved on its own, e.g. 'Portland = Portland, OR (PDX)'; tell the traveler

search.description: Route dict: origin, destination, names, destination_image, cabin, travelers, dates, trip_type, legs (multi-city), search_key, retrieved_at

search_url.description: slicktrip.com search page link with attribution

searched_as.description: What the search assumed: trip type, travelers, cabin

suggestions.description: On unknown_place: places to offer the traveler, each with code, name, kind (airport, all airports in the city, nearby airport), city, country

title: Search flights
